"Your blood tests show changes affecting your blood cells, liver and platelet count. This is a serious complication of pre-eclampsia called HELLP syndrome. It can worsen rapidly and can cause bleeding, liver complications, kidney problems and seizures. We need to monitor you very closely, stabilise your blood pressure, prevent seizures, monitor your blood results and assess your baby. Depending on your condition and the baby's condition, we may need to deliver the baby."

"I am concerned that this patient has HELLP syndrome, given the combination of haemolysis, elevated liver enzymes and thrombocytopenia. I would treat this as a severe obstetric complication and immediately involve senior obstetric, anaesthetic and haematology teams. I would stabilise her using an ABCDE approach, urgently control severe hypertension if present, administer magnesium sulfate for seizure prophylaxis where indicated, carefully manage fluids and monitor urine output. I would repeat FBC, renal and liver function, haemolysis and coagulation studies, group and crossmatch blood, and assess for DIC and hepatic complications. I would assess fetal wellbeing with CTG and ultrasound/Doppler where appropriate. I would then determine the safest timing and mode of delivery, with urgent delivery required if there is maternal or fetal deterioration. I would be particularly alert to severe RUQ pain with haemodynamic instability as a possible hepatic haematoma or rupture."
